title.zh: 卷十一 隋本紀上第十一: 高祖文帝
title.en: Volume 11 Sui Annals 1: Emperor Gau Wen
title.raw: 卷十一 隋本紀上第十一: 高祖文帝 Volume 11 Sui Annals 1: Emperor Gau Wen

sentences.zh: 高祖文帝

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu Wendi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu Wendi.

sentences.zh: 隋高祖文皇帝姓楊氏，諱堅，小名那羅延。

translations.literal: The Sui Emperor Gaozu Wendi bore the surname Yang; his taboo name was Jian, and his childhood name was Naluoyan.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui Founding Emperor Wen, surname Yang, taboo name Jian, childhood name Naluoyan.

sentences.zh: 本弘農華陰人，漢太尉震之十四世孫也。

translations.literal: He was originally a man of Huayin in Hongnong, the fourteenth-generation descendant of Zhen, Grand Commandant of Han.
translations.idiomatic: A native of Huayin in Hongnong, he was the fourteenth-generation descendant of Han Grand Commandant Zhen.

sentences.zh: 震八世孫，燕北平太守鉉。

translations.literal: Zhen's eighth-generation descendant was Xuan, Governor of Pingbei in Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Eight generations after Zhen came Xuan, Governor of Pingbei in Yan.

sentences.zh: 鉉子元壽，魏初為武川鎮司馬，因家於神武樹頹焉。

translations.literal: Xuan's son Yuanshou, in the early Wei, served as Military Administrator of Wuchuan Garrison and made his home at Shenwu Shuitui.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's son Yuanshou served as Military Administrator of Wuchuan Garrison in the early Wei and settled at Shenwu Shuitui.

sentences.zh: 元壽生太原太守惠嘏，嘏生平原太守烈，烈生寧遠將軍禎，禎生皇考忠。

translations.literal: Yuanshou begot Huigu, Governor of Taiyuan; Huigu begot Lie, Governor of Pingyuan; Lie begot Zhen, General Who Pacifies the Distance; Zhen begot the late Emperor's father, Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuanshou came Huigu, Governor of Taiyuan; from Huigu, Lie, Governor of Pingyuan; from Lie, Zhen, General Who Pacifies the Distance; and from Zhen, the late Emperor's father Zhong.

sentences.zh: 初，禎屬魏末喪亂，避地中山，結義徒以討鮮于修禮，遂死之。

translations.literal: At first, during the chaos at the end of Wei, Zhen fled to Zhongshan and gathered sworn followers to attack Xianyu Xiuli, and died in the effort.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei fell into chaos at the end of the dynasty, Zhen took refuge in Zhongshan, raised sworn followers against Xianyu Xiuli, and died in the fight.

sentences.zh: 周保定中，皇考著勛，追贈柱國大將軍、少保、興城郡公。

translations.literal: In the Baoding era of Zhou, because the late Emperor's father had performed meritorious service, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Pillar of State, Grand General, Junior Guardian, and Duke of Xingcheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou's Baoding era, the late Emperor's father was posthumously enfeoffed as Pillar of State, Grand General, Junior Guardian, and Duke of Xingcheng Commandery for his meritorious service.

sentences.zh: 皇考美須髯，身長七尺八寸，狀貌瑰偉，武藝絕倫；

translations.literal: The late Emperor's father had a fine beard; he stood seven feet eight inches tall, his appearance was magnificent, and his martial skill was unmatched;
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor's father wore a fine beard, stood seven feet eight inches tall, looked magnificent, and had martial skill beyond compare;

sentences.zh: 識量深重，有將率之略。

translations.literal: his judgment was deep and his capacity broad, and he possessed the strategic ability of a commander.
translations.idiomatic: his judgment ran deep, his capacity was broad, and he had the mind of a field commander.

sentences.zh: 年十八，客遊泰山，會梁兵陷郡國，沒江南。

translations.literal: At eighteen he traveled as a guest to Mount Tai; when Liang troops overran the commanderies and districts, he was captured in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he traveled to Mount Tai as a guest; when Liang armies overran the commanderies, he was taken captive in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 及北海王元顥入洛，乃與俱歸。

translations.literal: When Prince Yuan Hao of Beihai entered Luoyang, he returned together with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yuan Hao of Beihai entered Luoyang, he returned with him.

sentences.zh: 顥敗，爾朱度律召為帳下統軍。

translations.literal: When Hao was defeated, Erzhu Dulü summoned him to serve as a commander under his banner.
translations.idiomatic: After Hao's defeat, Erzhu Dulü summoned him to serve as a commander in his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 後從獨孤信，屢有軍功。

translations.literal: Later he followed Dugu Xin and repeatedly won military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Dugu Xin and won repeated distinction in battle.

sentences.zh: 又與信從魏孝武西遷。

translations.literal: He also followed Xin when Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Xin when Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved the court west.

sentences.zh: 東魏荊州刺史辛纂據穰城，皇考從信討之，與都督康洛兒、元長生乘城而入。

translations.literal: The Eastern Wei Governor of Jing Province, Xin Zuan, held Rang City; the late Emperor's father followed Xin to attack him and, with Commandants Kang Luo'er and Yuan Changsheng, scaled the wall and entered.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Wei Governor of Jing Province Xin Zuan held Rang City, the late Emperor's father followed Xin to attack him and, with Commandants Kang Luo'er and Yuan Changsheng, scaled the walls and entered.

sentences.zh: 彎弓大呼，斬纂以徇，城中懾服。

translations.literal: He bent his bow and shouted; he beheaded Zuan and displayed the head, and the city submitted in fear.
translations.idiomatic: He bent his bow and shouted, beheaded Zuan and displayed the head, and the city submitted in fear.

sentences.zh: 居半歲，以東魏之逼，與信俱歸。

translations.literal: After half a year, because of Eastern Wei pressure, he returned together with Xin.
translations.idiomatic: After half a year, pressed by Eastern Wei, he returned with Xin.

sentences.zh: 周文帝召居帳下。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou summoned him to serve under his banner.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou summoned him to serve in his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 嘗從周文狩於龍門，皇考獨當一猛獸，左挾其腰，右拔其舌，周文壯之。

translations.literal: Once, when he followed Emperor Wen on a hunt at Longmen, the late Emperor's father alone faced a fierce beast, seized it by the waist with his left hand and pulled out its tongue with his right; Emperor Wen admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Once on a hunt at Longmen with Emperor Wen, the late Emperor's father alone faced a fierce beast, seized it by the waist with his left hand and pulled out its tongue with his right; Emperor Wen was awed.

sentences.zh: 北臺謂猛獸為掩贍，因以字之。

translations.literal: The Northern Court called a fierce beast yanshan, and so gave him that style name.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Court called a fierce beast yanshan, and so gave him that style name.

sentences.zh: 從禽竇泰，破沙苑陣，封襄武縣公。

translations.literal: He followed the hunt against Dou Tai, broke the Shaya formation, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangwu County.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Dou Tai, broke the Shaya formation, and was enfeoffed Duke of Xiangwu County.

sentences.zh: 河橋之役，皇考與壯士五人力戰守橋，敵人不敢進。

translations.literal: In the battle at Heqiao, the late Emperor's father and five stalwart men fought hard to hold the bridge, and the enemy did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: At Heqiao, the late Emperor's father and five stalwart men fought to hold the bridge, and the enemy did not dare advance.

sentences.zh: 又與李遠破黑水稽胡，並與怡峰解玉壁圍，以功歷雲、洛二州刺史。

translations.literal: He also joined Li Yuan in defeating the Black Water Jiehu, and together with Yi Feng relieved the siege of Yubi; for his merit he served in succession as Governor of Yun and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined Li Yuan in defeating the Black Water Jiehu and, with Yi Feng, lifted the siege of Yubi; for this he served in turn as Governor of Yun and Luo.

sentences.zh: 芒山之戰，先登陷陣，除大都督。

translations.literal: In the battle at Mangshan he was first to ascend and break the enemy lines, and was appointed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: At Mangshan he was first to break the enemy lines, and was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 及侯景度江，梁氏喪敗。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze, the Liang house fell into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze, the Liang dynasty collapsed.

sentences.zh: 周文將經略，乃授皇考都督荊等十五州諸軍事，鎮穰城。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou planned a campaign of conquest and appointed the late Emperor's father Area Commander of the military affairs of Jing and fifteen other provinces, stationed at Rang City.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Wen of Zhou planned his conquest, he appointed the late Emperor's father Area Commander of the military affairs of Jing and fifteen other provinces, with his headquarters at Rang City.

sentences.zh: 梁雍州刺史、嶽陽王蕭察，雖曰稱籓，而尚懷貳心。

translations.literal: The Liang Governor of Yong Province and Prince of Yueyang, Xiao Cha, though he called himself a vassal, still harbored divided loyalties.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang Governor of Yong Province and Prince of Yueyang, Xiao Cha, though he called himself a vassal, still nursed divided loyalties.

sentences.zh: 皇考自樊城觀兵漢濱，易旗遞進。

translations.literal: The late Emperor's father reviewed troops at Fancheng and displayed his banners along the Han shore, advancing in relay.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor's father reviewed troops at Fancheng and sent his banners forward in relay along the Han shore.

sentences.zh: 實二千騎，察登樓望之，以為三萬，懼而服焉。

translations.literal: In reality there were two thousand horsemen; Cha climbed the tower to watch and thought there were thirty thousand, and in fear submitted.
translations.idiomatic: There were in truth only two thousand horsemen; Cha climbed the tower, thought he saw thirty thousand, and submitted in fear.

sentences.zh: 又攻梁隨郡，克之，獲其守桓和。

translations.literal: He also attacked the Liang commandery of Sui and took it, capturing its defender Huan He.
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked the Liang commandery of Sui, took it, and captured its defender Huan He.

sentences.zh: 所過城戍，望風請服。

translations.literal: The garrison cities he passed all requested submission at the sight of his banners.
translations.idiomatic: Every garrison city he passed requested submission at the sight of his banners.

sentences.zh: 進圍安陸。

translations.literal: He advanced to besiege Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to besiege Anlu.

sentences.zh: 梁同州刺史柳仲禮恐安陸不守，馳歸赴援。

translations.literal: The Liang Governor of Tong Province, Liu Zhongli, fearing Anlu could not be held, galloped back to bring relief.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhongli, Liang Governor of Tong Province, fearing Anlu could not be held, galloped back to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 諸將恐仲禮至則安陸難下，請急攻之。

translations.literal: The generals feared that if Zhongli arrived Anlu would be hard to take, and asked for an urgent assault.
translations.idiomatic: The generals feared that if Zhongli arrived Anlu would be hard to take and urged an immediate assault.

sentences.zh: 皇考曰：「仲禮已在近路，吾以奇兵襲之，一舉必克，則安陸不攻自拔，諸城可傳檄而定。

translations.literal: The late Emperor's father said, "Zhongli is already on the near road; if I strike him with surprise troops I am sure to take him in one blow, and then Anlu will fall without attack and the other cities can be settled by proclamation alone.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor's father said, "Zhongli is already on the near road; if I strike him with surprise troops I am sure to take him at one blow, and then Anlu will fall without a fight and the other cities can be settled by proclamation alone.

sentences.zh: 」於是選騎二千，銜枚夜進。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he selected two thousand horsemen and advanced by night with gags in their mouths.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he chose two thousand horsemen and advanced by night with gags in their mouths.

sentences.zh: 遇仲禮於漴頭，禽之，悉俘其眾。

translations.literal: He encountered Zhongli at Chongtou, captured him, and took all his men prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: He met Zhongli at Chongtou, captured him, and took all his men prisoner.

sentences.zh: 安陸、竟陵並降。

translations.literal: Anlu and Jingling both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Anlu and Jingling both surrendered.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝大懼，送子方略為質，並送載書，請魏以石城為限，梁以安陸為界。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang was greatly afraid; he sent his son Fanglue as a hostage and also sent a written pledge, asking that Wei take Shicheng as the boundary and Liang take Anlu as the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang was greatly afraid; he sent his son Fanglue as a hostage and a written pledge asking that Wei take Shicheng as the boundary and Liang take Anlu as the boundary.

sentences.zh: 皇考乃旋師。

translations.literal: The late Emperor's father then withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor's father then withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 進爵陳留郡公，位大將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced in rank to Duke of Chenliu Commandery and appointed Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Duke of Chenliu Commandery and appointed Grand General.

sentences.zh: 十七年，梁元帝逼其兄邵陵王綸。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Emperor Yuan of Liang pressed his elder brother, Prince Shaoling Lun.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, Emperor Yuan of Liang pressed his elder brother, Prince Shaoling Lun.

sentences.zh: 綸送質於齊，欲來寇。

translations.literal: Lun sent a hostage to Qi, intending to come and raid.
translations.idiomatic: Lun sent a hostage to Qi, intending to come raiding.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝密報周文。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang secretly reported this to Emperor Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang secretly reported this to Emperor Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 遣皇考討之。

translations.literal: He dispatched the late Emperor's father to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched the late Emperor's father to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 禽綸，數其罪，殺之。

translations.literal: He captured Lun, enumerated his crimes, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Lun, enumerated his crimes, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 初，皇考禽柳仲禮，遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: At first, when the late Emperor's father captured Liu Zhongli, he treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when the late Emperor's father captured Liu Zhongli, he treated him very generously.

sentences.zh: 仲禮至京，反譖皇考，言在軍大取金寶。

translations.literal: When Zhongli reached the capital, he turned and slandered the late Emperor's father, saying that in the army he had taken much gold and treasure.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongli reached the capital, he turned and slandered the late Emperor's father, saying that in the field he had seized much gold and treasure.

sentences.zh: 周文以皇考功重，不問。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou, because the late Emperor's father's merit was great, did not inquire into it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou, because the late Emperor's father's merit was great, did not inquire into it.

sentences.zh: 然皇考悔不殺仲禮，故至此殺綸。

translations.literal: Yet the late Emperor's father regretted not having killed Zhongli, and so on this occasion killed Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the late Emperor's father regretted not having killed Zhongli, and so on this occasion killed Lun.

sentences.zh: 皇考間歲再舉，盡定漢東地，甚得新附心。

translations.literal: The late Emperor's father twice campaigned within a year and fully settled the lands east of the Han, winning the hearts of the newly submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single year the late Emperor's father campaigned twice, fully settled the lands east of the Han, and won the hearts of the newly submitted.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝賜姓普六茹氏，行同州事。

translations.literal: Emperor Gong of Wei granted the surname Puliuru and put him in charge of the affairs of Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gong of Wei granted the surname Puliuru and put him in charge of the affairs of Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 及於謹伐江陵，皇考為前軍，屯江津，遏其走路。

translations.literal: When Yu Jin attacked Jiangling, the late Emperor's father served as vanguard, encamped at the Jin River, and blocked the enemy's escape route.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Jin attacked Jiangling, the late Emperor's father served as vanguard, encamped at the Jin River, and blocked the enemy's escape route.

sentences.zh: 梁人束刃於象鼻以戰，皇考射之，二象反走。

translations.literal: The men of Liang bound blades to elephants' trunks to fight; the late Emperor's father shot them, and the two elephants turned and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The men of Liang bound blades to elephants' trunks to fight; the late Emperor's father shot them, and the two elephants turned and fled.

sentences.zh: 江陵平，周文立蕭察為梁主，令皇考鎮穰城。

translations.literal: When Jiangling was pacified, Emperor Wen of Zhou installed Xiao Cha as ruler of Liang and ordered the late Emperor's father to garrison Rang City.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling was pacified, Emperor Wen of Zhou installed Xiao Cha as ruler of Liang and ordered the late Emperor's father to garrison Rang City.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔踐阼，入為小宗伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, the late Emperor's father entered the capital as Junior Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, the late Emperor's father entered the capital as Junior Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 及司馬消難請降，皇考與柱國達奚武援之。

translations.literal: When Sima Xiaonan requested surrender, the late Emperor's father joined Pillar of State Daxi Wu to reinforce him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Xiaonan requested surrender, the late Emperor's father joined Pillar of State Daxi Wu to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 入齊境五百里，前後遣三使報消難，皆不反命。

translations.literal: They entered Qi territory five hundred li; before and after, they sent three envoys to report to Xiaonan, and none returned with orders.
translations.idiomatic: They entered Qi territory five hundred li; before and after, they sent three envoys to report to Xiaonan, and none returned with orders.

sentences.zh: 及去北豫州三十里，武疑有變，欲還。

translations.literal: When they were thirty li from Northern Yuzhou, Wu suspected treachery and wished to turn back.
translations.idiomatic: When they were thirty li from Northern Yuzhou, Wu suspected treachery and wished to turn back.

sentences.zh: 皇考曰：「有進死，無退生。

translations.literal: The late Emperor's father said, "There is advance unto death, but no retreat unto life.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor's father said, "There is advance unto death, but no retreat unto life.

sentences.zh: 」獨以千騎，夜趣城下。

translations.literal: " He alone took a thousand horsemen and by night pressed to the foot of the city.
translations.idiomatic: " He alone took a thousand horsemen and by night pressed to the foot of the city.

sentences.zh: 候門開而入，乃馳遣召武。

translations.literal: He waited until the gate opened and entered, then galloped off to summon Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He waited until the gate opened and entered, then galloped off to summon Wu.

sentences.zh: 時齊鎮城伏敬遠勒甲士三千據東陴，舉烽嚴警。

translations.literal: At that time the Qi garrison commander Fu Jingyuan mustered three thousand armored soldiers and held the eastern wall, raising beacon fires in strict alarm.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Qi garrison commander Fu Jingyuan mustered three thousand armored soldiers and held the eastern wall, raising beacon fires in strict alarm.

sentences.zh: 武憚之，不欲保城，乃多取財寶，以消難先歸。

translations.literal: Wu feared him and did not wish to hold the city; he took much gold and treasure and had Xiaonan return first.
translations.idiomatic: Wu feared him and did not wish to hold the city; he took much gold and treasure and had Xiaonan return first.

sentences.zh: 皇考以三千騎殿，到洛南，皆解鞍而臥。

translations.literal: The late Emperor's father with three thousand horsemen served as rearguard; when they reached the south of Luo, all dismounted and lay down.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor's father with three thousand horsemen served as rearguard; when they reached the south of Luo, all dismounted and lay down.

sentences.zh: 齊眾來追，至於洛北。

translations.literal: The Qi host came in pursuit as far as the north of Luo.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi host came in pursuit as far as the north of Luo.

sentences.zh: 皇考謂將士曰：「但飽食，今在死地，賊必不敢度水。

translations.literal: The late Emperor's father said to his officers and men, "Eat your fill; we are now in a place of death, and the enemy will surely not dare cross the water.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor's father said to his officers and men, "Eat your fill; we are now in a place of death, and the enemy will surely not dare cross the water.

sentences.zh: 」食畢，齊兵陽若度水，皇考馳將擊之；

translations.literal: " When they had finished eating, the Qi troops feigned as if to cross the water; the late Emperor's father galloped forth to strike them;
translations.idiomatic: " When they had finished eating, the Qi troops feigned as if to cross the water; the late Emperor's father galloped forth to strike them;

sentences.zh: 齊兵不敢逼，遂徐引而還。

translations.literal: the Qi troops did not dare press close and so slowly withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: the Qi troops did not dare press close and so slowly withdrew.

sentences.zh: 武嘆曰：「達奚武自言是天下健兒，今日服矣。」

translations.literal: Wu sighed and said, "Daxi Wu calls himself the toughest man under heaven; today I yield to him."
translations.idiomatic: Wu sighed and said, "Daxi Wu calls himself the toughest man under heaven; today I yield to him."

sentences.zh: 進位柱國大將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced in rank to Pillar of State and Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Pillar of State and Grand General.

sentences.zh: 武成元年，進封隋國公，邑萬戶，別食竟陵縣一千戶，收其租賦。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wucheng, he was further enfeoffed as Duke of Sui with a fief of ten thousand households, separately granted the tax revenue of one thousand households of Jingling County, and allowed to collect its rents and levies.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wucheng he was further enfeoffed Duke of Sui with a fief of ten thousand households, separately granted the tax revenue of one thousand households of Jingling County, and allowed to collect its rents and levies.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，為大司空。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding, he became Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoding he became Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 時朝議與突厥伐齊。

translations.literal: At that time the court deliberated on joining with the Turks to attack Qi.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court deliberated on joining with the Turks to attack Qi.

sentences.zh: 公卿咸以齊兵強國富，斛律明月不易可當，兵非十萬眾不可。

translations.literal: The ministers all considered Qi's troops strong and the state rich, and that Hulu Mingyue was not easily matched; they said no fewer than one hundred thousand troops would do.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all considered Qi's troops strong and the state rich, and that Hulu Mingyue was not easily matched; they said no fewer than one hundred thousand troops would do.

sentences.zh: 皇考獨曰：「萬騎足矣，明月豎子，亦何能為！

translations.literal: The late Emperor's father alone said, "Ten thousand horsemen are enough; what can that stripling Mingyue do!
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor's father alone said, "Ten thousand horsemen are enough; what can that stripling Mingyue do!

sentences.zh: 」三年，乃以皇考為元帥，大將軍楊纂、李穆、王傑、爾朱敏及開府元壽、田弘、慕容近等皆隸焉。

translations.literal: " In the third year he was made supreme commander; Grand Generals Yang Zuan, Li Mu, Wang Jie, Erzhu Min, and Palace Gate Generals Yuan Shou, Tian Hong, Murong Jin, and others were all placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: " In the third year he was made supreme commander; Grand Generals Yang Zuan, Li Mu, Wang Jie, Erzhu Min, and Palace Gate Generals Yuan Shou, Tian Hong, Murong Jin, and others were all placed under him.

sentences.zh: 又令達奚武帥步騎三萬自南道進，期會晉陽。

translations.literal: He also ordered Daxi Wu to lead thirty thousand infantry and cavalry by the southern route to join forces at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Daxi Wu to lead thirty thousand infantry and cavalry by the southern route to join forces at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 皇考乃留敏據什賁，遊兵河上。

translations.literal: The late Emperor's father then left Min to hold Shiben and sent roaming troops along the river.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor's father then left Min to hold Shiben and sent roaming troops along the river.

sentences.zh: 皇考出武川，過故宅，祭先人，饗將士，度卷二十餘城。

translations.literal: The late Emperor's father marched out of Wuchuan, passed his former home, sacrificed to his ancestors, feasted his officers and men, and crossed more than twenty walled places.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor's father marched out of Wuchuan, passed his former home, sacrificed to his ancestors, feasted his officers and men, and crossed more than twenty walled places.

sentences.zh: 齊人守陘嶺之隘，皇考縱奇兵大破之，留楊纂屯靈丘為後拒。

translations.literal: The Qi held the narrow pass at Shanling; the late Emperor's father routed them with surprise troops and left Yang Zuan to garrison Lingqiu as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi held the narrow pass at Shanling; the late Emperor's father routed them with surprise troops and left Yang Zuan to garrison Lingqiu as rear guard.

sentences.zh: 突厥木桿可汗控地頭可汗、步離可汗等，以十萬騎來會。

translations.literal: The Turkic Khan Muhan, together with Khans Kedou and Buli and others, came to join him with one hundred thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: The Turkic Khan Muhan, together with Khans Kedou and Buli and others, came to join him with one hundred thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 四年正月朔，攻晉陽。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the fourth year, he attacked Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the first month of the fourth year, he attacked Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 時大雪風寒，齊人乃悉其精銳，鼓噪而出。

translations.literal: At that time snow fell heavily and the wind was bitterly cold; the Qi mustered all their elite troops and came out shouting and clamoring.
translations.idiomatic: At that time snow fell heavily and the wind was bitterly cold; the Qi mustered all their elite troops and came out shouting and clamoring.

sentences.zh: 突厥引上西山，不肯戰，眾失色。

translations.literal: The Turks withdrew up the western mountain and refused to fight; the troops turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks withdrew up the western mountain and refused to fight; the troops turned pale.

sentences.zh: 皇考乃率七百人步戰，死者十四五。

translations.literal: The late Emperor's father then led seven hundred men in infantry combat; four or five out of ten died.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor's father then led seven hundred men in infantry combat; four or five out of ten died.

sentences.zh: 以武后期，乃班師。

translations.literal: Because Wu was late, he withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wu was late, he withdrew the army.

sentences.zh: 齊人亦不敢逼。

translations.literal: The Qi also did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi also did not dare press close.

sentences.zh: 突厥乃縱兵大掠。

translations.literal: The Turks then let their troops plunder on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks then let their troops plunder on a great scale.

sentences.zh: 自晉陽至平城，七百餘里，人畜無遺。

translations.literal: From Jinyang to Pingcheng, more than seven hundred li, neither man nor beast was left.
translations.idiomatic: From Jinyang to Pingcheng, more than seven hundred li, neither man nor beast was left.

sentences.zh: 周武帝拜皇考為太傅，晉公護以其不附己，以為涇州總管。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou appointed the late Emperor's father Grand Tutor; Duke Hu of Jin, because he did not attach himself to him, made him Area Commander of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou appointed the late Emperor's father Grand Tutor; Duke Hu of Jin, because he did not attach himself to him, made him Area Commander of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 是歲，大軍又東伐，晉公護出洛陽，令皇考出沃野，以應接突厥。

translations.literal: That year the great army again marched east; Duke Hu of Jin went out from Luoyang and ordered the late Emperor's father to go out from Woye to link up with the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: That year the great army again marched east; Duke Hu of Jin went out from Luoyang and ordered the late Emperor's father to go out from Woye to link up with the Turks.

sentences.zh: 時軍糧少，諸將憂之。

translations.literal: At that time army provisions were few and the generals were worried.
translations.idiomatic: At that time army provisions were few and the generals were worried.

sentences.zh: 皇考曰：「當獲以濟事耳。

translations.literal: The late Emperor's father said, "We shall obtain enough to see the affair through.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor's father said, "We shall obtain enough to see the affair through.

sentences.zh: 」乃招誘稽胡首領，咸令在坐，使王傑盛軍容鳴鼓而出。

translations.literal: " He then summoned and enticed the Jiehu chieftains, had them all take their seats, and had Wang Jie display the army in full array and beat drums as he marched out.
translations.idiomatic: " He then summoned and enticed the Jiehu chieftains, had them all take their seats, and had Wang Jie display the army in full array and beat drums as he marched out.

sentences.zh: 皇考陽怪問之。

translations.literal: The late Emperor's father feigned surprise and asked about it.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor's father feigned surprise and asked about it.

sentences.zh: 傑曰：「大冢宰已至洛陽，天子聞銀、夏間胡擾動，故使傑就攻除之。

translations.literal: Jie said, "The Grand Preceptor has already reached Luoyang; the Son of Heaven heard that the Hu between Yin and Xia were stirring, and so sent Jie to attack and eliminate them.
translations.idiomatic: Jie said, "The Grand Preceptor has already reached Luoyang; the Son of Heaven heard that the Hu between Yin and Xia were stirring, and so sent Jie to attack and eliminate them.

sentences.zh: 」又令突厥使者馳告曰：「可汗更入并州，留兵馬十萬在長城下，故令問公，若有稽胡不服，欲來共破之。

translations.literal: " He also had a Turkic envoy gallop off to announce, "The Khan is entering Bing Province again and has left one hundred thousand troops and horses below the Great Wall, and so sends me to ask you: if any Jiehu refuse submission, he wishes to come and destroy them together with you.
translations.idiomatic: " He also had a Turkic envoy gallop off to announce, "The Khan is entering Bing Province again and has left one hundred thousand troops and horses below the Great Wall, and so sends me to ask you: if any Jiehu refuse submission, he wishes to come and destroy them together with you.

sentences.zh: 」坐者皆懼。

translations.literal: " All who were seated were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: " All who were seated were afraid.

sentences.zh: 皇考慰喻遣之，於是歸命，饋輸填積。

translations.literal: The late Emperor's father comforted and instructed them and sent them away; thereupon they submitted, and tribute and supplies piled up.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor's father comforted and instructed them and sent them away; thereupon they submitted, and tribute and supplies piled up.

sentences.zh: 屬晉公護先退，皇考亦罷兵而還鎮。

translations.literal: Because Duke Hu of Jin had already withdrawn first, the late Emperor's father also ceased campaigning and returned to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Because Duke Hu of Jin had already withdrawn first, the late Emperor's father also ceased campaigning and returned to his garrison.

sentences.zh: 又以政績稱，詔賜錢三十萬，布五百匹，谷二千斛。

translations.literal: Again because of distinguished administrative achievement, an edict granted him three hundred thousand cash, five hundred bolts of cloth, and two thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Again for distinguished administrative achievement, an edict granted him three hundred thousand cash, five hundred bolts of cloth, and two thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 以疾還京，周武及晉公護屢臨視焉。

translations.literal: Because of illness he returned to the capital; Emperor Wu of Zhou and Duke Hu of Jin repeatedly came to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Ill, he returned to the capital; Emperor Wu of Zhou and Duke Hu of Jin repeatedly came to visit him.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈太保、都督同朔等十三州軍事、同州刺史，本官如故。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was granted Grand Guardian, Area Commander of the military affairs of Tong, Shuo, and twelve other provinces, and Governor of Tong Province, his original office unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted Grand Guardian, Area Commander of the military affairs of Tong, Shuo, and twelve other provinces, and Governor of Tong Province, his original office unchanged.

sentences.zh: 謚曰桓公。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Duke Huan.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Duke Huan.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，追尊為武元皇帝，廟號太祖。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang, he was posthumously honored as Emperor Wuyuan, with temple name Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaihuang he was posthumously honored as Emperor Wuyuan, with temple name Taizu.

sentences.zh: 帝，武元皇帝之長子也。

translations.literal: The Emperor was the eldest son of Emperor Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was the eldest son of Emperor Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 皇妣曰呂氏。

translations.literal: The imperial mother was the Lady Lü.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial mother was the Lady Lü.

sentences.zh: 以周大統七年六月癸丑夜，生帝於馮翊波若寺。

translations.literal: On the night of the day guichou in the sixth month of the seventh year of Datong of Zhou, the Emperor was born at Boruo Temple in Fenyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of guichou in the sixth month of Datong year seven of Zhou, the Emperor was born at Boruo Temple in Fenyang.

sentences.zh: 有紫氣充庭。

translations.literal: Purple vapor filled the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Purple vapor filled the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 時有尼來自河東，謂皇妣曰：「此兒所從來甚異，不可於俗間處之。

translations.literal: At that time a nun came from Hedong and said to the imperial mother, "This child's origin is very unusual; he cannot be kept among ordinary people.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a nun came from Hedong and said to the imperial mother, "This child's origin is very unusual; he cannot be kept among ordinary people.

sentences.zh: 」乃將帝舍於別館，躬自撫養。

translations.literal: " She then lodged the Emperor in a separate residence and personally nursed him.
translations.idiomatic: " She then lodged the Emperor in a separate residence and personally nursed him.

sentences.zh: 皇妣抱帝，忽見頭上出角，遍體起鱗，墜帝於地。

translations.literal: The imperial mother held the Emperor and suddenly saw horns emerge from his head and scales rise over his whole body; she dropped the Emperor to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial mother held the Emperor and suddenly saw horns emerge from his head and scales rise over his whole body; she dropped the Emperor to the ground.

sentences.zh: 尼自外見，曰：「已驚我兒，致令晚得天下。

translations.literal: The nun, seeing from outside, said, "You have startled my child and will make him obtain the realm late.
translations.idiomatic: The nun, seeing from outside, said, "You have startled my child and will make him obtain the realm late.

sentences.zh: 」帝龍頷，額上有五柱入頂，目光外射；

translations.literal: " The Emperor had a dragon jaw; on his forehead five pillars entered the crown, and his gaze shot outward;
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor had a dragon jaw; on his forehead five pillars entered the crown, and his gaze shot outward;

sentences.zh: 有文在手曰「王」字，長上短下，沈深嚴重。

translations.literal: on his hand was a mark reading the character "King"; he was tall above and short below, deep, grave, and solemn.
translations.idiomatic: on his hand was a mark reading the character "King"; he was tall above and short below, deep, grave, and solemn.

sentences.zh: 初入太學，雖至親昵，不敢狎也。

translations.literal: When he first entered the Imperial Academy, even those closest to him did not dare treat him lightly.
translations.idiomatic: When he first entered the Imperial Academy, even those closest to him did not dare treat him lightly.

sentences.zh: 年十四，京兆尹薛善辟為功曹。

translations.literal: At fourteen, Prefect of Jingzhao Xue Shan appointed him Clerk for Merit.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen, Prefect of Jingzhao Xue Shan appointed him Clerk for Merit.

sentences.zh: 十五，以皇考勛，授散騎常侍、車騎大將軍、儀同三司，封成紀縣公。

translations.literal: At fifteen, because of the late Emperor's father's merit, he was appointed Attendant Cavalier, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Third Rank Equivalent, and enfeoffed Duke of Chengji County.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen, because of the late Emperor's father's merit, he was appointed Attendant Cavalier, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Third Rank Equivalent, and enfeoffed Duke of Chengji County.

sentences.zh: 十六，遷驃騎大將軍，加開府。

translations.literal: At sixteen, he was transferred to General of Agile Cavalry and given an open office.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen, he was transferred to General of Agile Cavalry and given an open office.

sentences.zh: 周文帝見而嘆曰：「此兒風骨，非世間人。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou saw him and sighed, saying, "This boy's bearing is not of this world.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou saw him and sighed, saying, "This boy's bearing is not of this world.

sentences.zh: 」明帝即位，授右小宗伯，進封大興郡公。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, he was appointed Junior Director of the Right Imperial Clan and advanced to Duke of Daxing Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, he was appointed Junior Director of the Right Imperial Clan and advanced to Duke of Daxing Commandery.

sentences.zh: 明帝嘗遣善相者來和視帝。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming once sent a skilled physiognomist named Lai He to examine the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming once sent a skilled physiognomist named Lai He to examine the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 和詭對曰：「不過柱國。

translations.literal: He deceptively replied, "No higher than Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: He deceptively replied, "No higher than Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 」既而私謂帝曰：「公當為天下君，必大誅殺而後定。」

translations.literal: " Later he privately told the Emperor, "Your Grace will become ruler of the realm; there must be great slaughter before it is settled."
translations.idiomatic: " Later he privately told the Emperor, "Your Grace will become ruler of the realm; there must be great slaughter before it is settled."

sentences.zh: 周武帝即位，遷左小宮伯，出為隨州刺史，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou ascended the throne, he was transferred to Junior Director of the Left Palace and sent out as Governor of Sui Province, advanced to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou ascended the throne, he was transferred to Junior Director of the Left Palace and sent out as Governor of Sui Province, advanced to Grand General.

sentences.zh: 後征還，遇皇妣寢疾三年，晝夜不離左右，以純孝稱。

translations.literal: Later he was recalled; when the imperial mother fell gravely ill for three years, he did not leave her side day or night, and was famed for pure filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was recalled; when the imperial mother fell gravely ill for three years, he did not leave her side day or night, and was famed for pure filial piety.

sentences.zh: 宇文護執政，尤忌帝，屢將害焉。

translations.literal: Yuwen Hu held power and especially feared the Emperor, repeatedly intending to harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu held power and especially feared the Emperor, repeatedly intending to harm him.

sentences.zh: 賴大將軍侯伏侯壽等救護以免。

translations.literal: He was saved from harm thanks to Grand General Hou Fuhou Shou and others who protected him.
translations.idiomatic: He was saved from harm thanks to Grand General Hou Fuhou Shou and others who protected him.

sentences.zh: 後襲爵隋國公。

translations.literal: Later he inherited the title Duke of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Later he inherited the title Duke of Sui.

sentences.zh: 周武既為皇太子娉帝長女為妃，益加禮重。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Wu of Zhou had taken the Emperor's eldest daughter as consort for the crown prince, he was treated with even greater honor.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Wu of Zhou had taken the Emperor's eldest daughter as consort for the crown prince, he was treated with even greater honor.

sentences.zh: 齊王憲言於周武曰：「普六茹堅相貌，臣每見之，不覺自失。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Qi said to Emperor Wu of Zhou, "Puliuru Jian's appearance—each time I see him I lose myself without knowing it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Qi said to Emperor Wu of Zhou, "Puliuru Jian's appearance—each time I see him I lose myself without knowing it.

sentences.zh: 恐非人下，請早除之。」

translations.literal: I fear he is not meant to serve under others; please remove him early."
translations.idiomatic: I fear he is not meant to serve under others; please remove him early."

sentences.zh: 周武曰：「此止可為將耳。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou said, "He can only be a general.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou said, "He can only be a general.

sentences.zh: 」內史王軌驟諫曰：「皇太子非社稷主，普六茹堅有反相。

translations.literal: " Palace Secretary Wang Gui suddenly remonstrated, saying, "The crown prince is not fit to be lord of the altars of soil and grain; Puliuru Jian has the look of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: " Palace Secretary Wang Gui suddenly remonstrated, saying, "The crown prince is not fit to be lord of the altars of soil and grain; Puliuru Jian has the look of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 」周武不悅曰：「必天命，將若之何？

translations.literal: " Emperor Wu of Zhou, displeased, said, "If it is Heaven's mandate, what can be done?
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Wu of Zhou, displeased, said, "If it is Heaven's mandate, what can be done?

sentences.zh: 」帝甚懼，深自晦匿。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was greatly afraid and deeply concealed himself.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was greatly afraid and deeply concealed himself.

sentences.zh: 後從周武平齊，進柱國。

translations.literal: Later he followed Emperor Wu of Zhou in pacifying Qi and was advanced to Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Emperor Wu of Zhou in pacifying Qi and was advanced to Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 又與齊王憲破齊任城王湝於冀州，除定州總管。

translations.literal: He also joined Prince Xian of Qi in defeating Prince Rencheng Huo of Qi at Ji Province and was appointed Area Commander of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined Prince Xian of Qi in defeating Prince Rencheng Huo of Qi at Ji Province and was appointed Area Commander of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 先是州城門久閉不行，齊人白：「文宣時，或請開之，文宣不許，曰：『當有聖人啟之。

translations.literal: Earlier the city gate had long been closed and not used; the men of Qi reported, "In the time of Emperor Wenxuan, some asked to open it; Wenxuan would not allow it, saying, 'A sage will open it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the city gate had long been closed and not used; the men of Qi reported, "In the time of Emperor Wenxuan, some asked to open it; Wenxuan would not allow it, saying, 'A sage will open it.

sentences.zh: 』」及帝至而開之，莫不驚異。

translations.literal: '" When the Emperor arrived and opened it, all were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: '" When the Emperor arrived and opened it, all were astonished.

sentences.zh: 遷亳州總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Area Commander of Bo Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Area Commander of Bo Province.

sentences.zh: 周宣帝即位，以后父，徵拜上柱國、大司馬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan of Zhou ascended the throne, because he was the empress's father, he was summoned and appointed Pillar of State and Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan of Zhou ascended the throne, because he was the empress's father, he was summoned and appointed Pillar of State and Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 大象初，遷太后丞、右司武，俄轉大前疑。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daxiang, he was transferred to Assistant to the Empress Dowager and Director of Martial Affairs on the Right, and soon after became Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daxiang, he was transferred to Assistant to the Empress Dowager and Director of Martial Affairs on the Right, and soon after became Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 周宣每巡幸，恒委以居守。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Xuan toured on inspection, he always entrusted him to remain and guard.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Xuan toured on inspection, he always entrusted him to remain and guard.

sentences.zh: 時周宣為《刑經聖制》，其法深刻，帝以法令滋章，非興化之道，切諫，不納。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xuan had the Criminal Canon of Sacred Governance; its laws were harsh and deep; the Emperor, because laws and edicts were multiplying and this was not the way to promote transformation, remonstrated urgently, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Xuan had the Criminal Canon of Sacred Governance; its laws were harsh and deep; the Emperor, because laws and edicts were multiplying and this was not the way to promote transformation, remonstrated urgently, but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 帝位望益隆，周宣頗以為忌。

translations.literal: The Emperor's position and reputation grew ever higher, and Emperor Xuan came to view him with suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's position and reputation grew ever higher, and Emperor Xuan came to view him with suspicion.

sentences.zh: 時周宣四幸女並為皇后，爭寵相毀。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xuan's four favored women were all made empresses and competed for favor, slandering one another.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Xuan's four favored women were all made empresses and competed for favor, slandering one another.

sentences.zh: 周宣每謂后曰：「必族滅爾家。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan often said to the empress, "I shall exterminate your whole clan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan often said to the empress, "I shall exterminate your whole clan.

sentences.zh: 」因召帝，命左右曰：「若色動，即殺之。

translations.literal: " He then summoned the Emperor and ordered those at his side, "If his expression changes, kill him at once.
translations.idiomatic: " He then summoned the Emperor and ordered those at his side, "If his expression changes, kill him at once.

sentences.zh: 」帝容色自若，遂免。

translations.literal: " The Emperor's countenance remained calm, and so he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor's countenance remained calm, and so he was spared.

sentences.zh: 大象二年五月，以帝為揚州總管，將發，暴足疾而止。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Daxiang, the Emperor was made Area Commander of Yang Province; as he was about to depart, he suddenly fell ill with a foot ailment and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Daxiang, the Emperor was made Area Commander of Yang Province; as he was about to depart, he suddenly fell ill with a foot ailment and stopped.

sentences.zh: 乙未，周宣不悆。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, Emperor Xuan fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yiwei, Emperor Xuan fell ill.

sentences.zh: 時靜帝幼沖，前內史上大夫鄭譯、禦正大夫劉昉以帝皇后之父，眾望所集，遂矯詔引帝入侍疾。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Jing was young; former Senior Palace Secretary Zheng Yi and Director of Correct Governance Liu Fang, because the Emperor was the empress's father and the focus of public expectation, forged an edict summoning the Emperor to attend the illness.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Jing was young; former Senior Palace Secretary Zheng Yi and Director of Correct Governance Liu Fang, because the Emperor was the empress's father and the focus of public expectation, forged an edict summoning the Emperor to attend the illness.

sentences.zh: 因受遺輔政，都督內外諸軍事。

translations.literal: He thereby received the testamentary charge to assist in government and was made Area Commander of all military affairs within and without.
translations.idiomatic: He thereby received the testamentary charge to assist in government and was made Area Commander of all military affairs within and without.

sentences.zh: 帝恐周氏諸王在籓生變，稱趙王招將嫁女於突厥為詞以征之。

translations.literal: The Emperor feared the Zhou princes in the provinces would raise trouble and, on the pretext that Prince Zhao of Zhao was about to marry his daughter to the Turks, summoned them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor feared the Zhou princes in the provinces would raise trouble and, on the pretext that Prince Zhao of Zhao was about to marry his daughter to the Turks, summoned them.

sentences.zh: 己酉，周宣崩。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou, Emperor Xuan died.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiyou, Emperor Xuan died.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，靜帝詔假黃鉞、左大丞相，百官總己而聽焉。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, Emperor Jing issued an edict granting the yellow battle-axe and appointing him Left Grand Chancellor; all officials were to obey his orders.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengxu, Emperor Jing issued an edict granting the yellow battle-axe and appointing him Left Grand Chancellor; all officials were to obey his orders.

sentences.zh: 以正陽宮為丞相府，以鄭譯為長史，劉悆昉為司馬，具置僚佐。

translations.literal: The Zhengyang Palace was made the chancellor's office; Zheng Yi was made Chief Administrator, Liu Fang was made Chief of Staff, and a full staff was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhengyang Palace was made the chancellor's office; Zheng Yi was made Chief Administrator, Liu Fang was made Chief of Staff, and a full staff was appointed.

sentences.zh: 周宣時刑政峻酷者，悉更以寬大之制，天下歸心矣。

translations.literal: The harsh and cruel punishments and government of Emperor Xuan's time were all changed to lenient systems, and the realm turned its heart to him.
translations.idiomatic: The harsh and cruel punishments and government of Emperor Xuan's time were all changed to lenient systems, and the realm turned its heart to him.

sentences.zh: 六月，趙王招、陳王純、趙王盛、代王達、滕王悄並至長安。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Prince Zhao of Zhao, Prince Chun of Chen, Prince Sheng of Zhao, Prince Da of Dai, and Prince Qiao of Teng all arrived at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Prince Zhao of Zhao, Prince Chun of Chen, Prince Sheng of Zhao, Prince Da of Dai, and Prince Qiao of Teng all arrived at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 相州總管尉遲迥自以宿將，至是不能平，遂舉兵。

translations.literal: Area Commander of Xiang Province Yuchi Jiong, considering himself a veteran general, could not accept this and so raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: Area Commander of Xiang Province Yuchi Jiong, considering himself a veteran general, could not accept this and so raised troops.

sentences.zh: 趙、魏之士響應，旬日間，眾至十餘萬。

translations.literal: Men of Zhao and Wei responded; within ten days the host reached more than one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Men of Zhao and Wei responded; within ten days the host reached more than one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 宇文胄以滎州，石悆以建州，席毗以沛郡，毗弟叉羅以兗州，皆應。

translations.literal: Yuwen Zhou held Ying Province, Shi Yu held Jian Province, Xi Pi held Pei Commandery, and Pi's younger brother Chaluo held Yan Province; all responded.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Zhou held Ying Province, Shi Yu held Jian Province, Xi Pi held Pei Commandery, and Pi's younger brother Chaluo held Yan Province; all responded.

sentences.zh: 迥遣子質於陳，以求援。

translations.literal: Jiong sent his son Zhi to Chen to seek aid.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong sent his son Zhi to Chen to seek aid.

sentences.zh: 帝命上柱國、鄖公韋孝寬討之。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Pillar of State Duke Wei Xiaokuan of Yun to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Pillar of State Duke Wei Xiaokuan of Yun to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 雍州牧、畢王賢及趙、陳等五王謀作亂，帝執賢斬之，而掩趙王等罪。

translations.literal: Governor of Yong Province Prince Xian of Bi and the five princes Zhao, Chen, and others plotted rebellion; the Emperor seized Xian and executed him, while concealing the crimes of Prince Zhao and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Yong Province Prince Xian of Bi and the five princes Zhao, Chen, and others plotted rebellion; the Emperor seized Xian and executed him, while concealing the crimes of Prince Zhao and the others.

sentences.zh: 因詔五王劍履上殿。

translations.literal: He then issued an edict allowing the five princes to wear swords and shoes in the palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an edict allowing the five princes to wear swords and shoes in the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 入朝不趨，以安之。

translations.literal: They need not hurry when entering court, to reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: They need not hurry when entering court, to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 時五王陰謀滋甚，帝以酒肴造趙王，觀其指。

translations.literal: At that time the five princes' secret plots grew ever deeper; the Emperor brought wine and food to Prince Zhao to observe his intentions.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the five princes' secret plots grew ever deeper; the Emperor brought wine and food to Prince Zhao to observe his intentions.

sentences.zh: 趙王伏甲於臥內，帝賴元胄以免，於是誅趙、越二王。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao hid armed men in his bedchamber; the Emperor was saved thanks to Yuan Zhou, and thereupon the princes of Zhao and Yue were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhao hid armed men in his bedchamber; the Emperor was saved thanks to Yuan Zhou, and thereupon the princes of Zhao and Yue were executed.

sentences.zh: 八月庚午，韋孝寬破尉遲迥，斬之，傳首闕下，余黨悉平。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu of the eighth month, Wei Xiaokuan defeated Yuchi Jiong, beheaded him, sent the head to the palace gate, and all remaining partisans were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengwu of the eighth month, Wei Xiaokuan defeated Yuchi Jiong, beheaded him, sent the head to the palace gate, and all remaining partisans were pacified.

sentences.zh: 初，迥之亂，鄖州總管司馬消難據州應迥，淮南州縣多從之。

translations.literal: At first, during Jiong's rebellion, Area Commander of Yun Province Sima Xiaonan held the province in response to Jiong, and many districts south of the Huai responded.
translations.idiomatic: At first, during Jiong's rebellion, Area Commander of Yun Province Sima Xiaonan held the province in response to Jiong, and many districts south of the Huai responded.

sentences.zh: 襄州總管王誼討之，消難奔陳。

translations.literal: Area Commander of Xiang Province Wang Yi attacked him, and Xiaonan fled to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Area Commander of Xiang Province Wang Yi attacked him, and Xiaonan fled to Chen.

sentences.zh: 荊、郢群蠻乘釁而起，命亳州總管賀若誼討平之。

translations.literal: The tribal peoples of Jing and Ying seized the opportunity to rise; the Emperor ordered Area Commander of Bo Province He Ruo Yi to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal peoples of Jing and Ying seized the opportunity to rise; the Emperor ordered Area Commander of Bo Province He Ruo Yi to suppress and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 先是，上柱國王謙為益州總管，亦擁眾邑、蜀，以匡復為辭。

translations.literal: Earlier, Pillar of State Wang Qian was Area Commander of Yi Province and also gathered troops in Yi and Shu, using restoration as his pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Pillar of State Wang Qian was Area Commander of Yi Province and also gathered troops in Yi and Shu, using restoration as his pretext.

sentences.zh: 帝以東夏、山南為事，未遑致討，謙遂屯劍口，陷始州。

translations.literal: The Emperor, occupied with affairs in eastern Xia and south of the mountains, had no leisure to attack him; Qian then encamped at Jiankou and took Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, occupied with affairs in eastern Xia and south of the mountains, had no leisure to attack him; Qian then encamped at Jiankou and took Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 至是，乃命上柱國梁睿討平之，傳首闕下。

translations.literal: At this time he ordered Pillar of State Liang Rui to suppress and pacify him and sent the head to the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: At this time he ordered Pillar of State Liang Rui to suppress and pacify him and sent the head to the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 隳劍閣之險，以絕好亂之萌焉。

translations.literal: The peril of Jiange was destroyed to cut off the seeds of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The peril of Jiange was destroyed to cut off the seeds of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 九月壬子，周帝進帝大丞相。

translations.literal: On the day renzi of the ninth month, the Zhou emperor advanced the Emperor to Grand Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renzi of the ninth month, the Zhou emperor advanced the Emperor to Grand Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 十月，周帝詔追贈皇曾祖烈為柱國、太保、都督十州諸軍事、徐州刺史、隋國公，謚曰康。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the Zhou emperor issued an edict posthumously enfeoffing the imperial great-grandfather Lie as Pillar of State, Grand Guardian, Area Commander of the military affairs of ten provinces, Governor of Xu Province, and Duke of Sui, with posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, the Zhou emperor issued an edict posthumously enfeoffing the imperial great-grandfather Lie as Pillar of State, Grand Guardian, Area Commander of the military affairs of ten provinces, Governor of Xu Province, and Duke of Sui, with posthumous title Kang.

sentences.zh: 皇祖禎為柱國、都督十三州諸軍事、同州刺史、隋國公，謚曰獻。

translations.literal: The imperial grandfather Zhen was enfeoffed as Pillar of State, Area Commander of the military affairs of thirteen provinces, Governor of Tong Province, and Duke of Sui, with posthumous title Xian.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial grandfather Zhen was enfeoffed as Pillar of State, Area Commander of the military affairs of thirteen provinces, Governor of Tong Province, and Duke of Sui, with posthumous title Xian.

sentences.zh: 皇考忠為上柱國、太師、大冢宰、都督十三州諸軍事、雍州牧。

translations.literal: The late Emperor's father Zhong was enfeoffed as Pillar of State, Grand Preceptor, Grand Preceptor of State, Area Commander of the military affairs of thirteen provinces, and Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor's father Zhong was enfeoffed as Pillar of State, Grand Preceptor, Grand Preceptor of State, Area Commander of the military affairs of thirteen provinces, and Governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，誅陳王純。

translations.literal: On the day renxu, Prince Chun of Chen was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renxu, Prince Chun of Chen was executed.

sentences.zh: 周帝進帝大冢宰，五府總於天官。

translations.literal: The Zhou emperor advanced the Emperor to Grand Preceptor of State; the five offices were all placed under the Celestial Minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor advanced the Emperor to Grand Preceptor of State; the five offices were all placed under the Celestial Minister.

sentences.zh: 十一月辛未，誅代王達、滕王悄。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei of the eleventh month, Prince Da of Dai and Prince Qiao of Teng were executed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinwei of the eleventh month, Prince Da of Dai and Prince Qiao of Teng were executed.

sentences.zh: 十二月甲子，周帝授帝相國，總百揆，去都督內外諸軍事、大冢宰之號，進爵為王。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi of the twelfth month, the Zhou emperor appointed the Emperor Chancellor of State, in charge of all affairs; the titles Area Commander of all military affairs within and without and Grand Preceptor of State were removed, and he was advanced in rank to king.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi of the twelfth month, the Zhou emperor appointed the Emperor Chancellor of State, in charge of all affairs; the titles Area Commander of all military affairs within and without and Grand Preceptor of State were removed, and he was advanced in rank to king.

sentences.zh: 以隋州之崇業，鄖州之安陸、城陽，溫州之宜人，應州之平靖、上明，順州之淮南，士州之永川，昌州之廣昌、安昌，申州之義陽、淮安，息州之新蔡、建安，豫州之汝南、臨潁、廣寧、初安，蔡州之蔡陽，郢州之漢東二十郡為隋國。

translations.literal: The twenty commanderies of Chongye in Sui Province; Anlu and Chengyang in Yun Province; Yiren in Wen Province; Pingjing and Shangming in Ying Province; Huainan in Shun Province; Yongchuan in Shi Province; Guangchang and Anchang in Chang Province; Yiyang and Huai'an in Shen Province; Xincai and Jian'an in Xi Province; Runan, Linying, Guangning, and Chuan in Yu Province; Caiyang in Cai Province; and Handong in Ying Province were made the state of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty commanderies of Chongye in Sui Province; Anlu and Chengyang in Yun Province; Yiren in Wen Province; Pingjing and Shangming in Ying Province; Huainan in Shun Province; Yongchuan in Shi Province; Guangchang and Anchang in Chang Province; Yiyang and Huai'an in Shen Province; Xincai and Jian'an in Xi Province; Runan, Linying, Guangning, and Chuan in Yu Province; Caiyang in Cai Province; and Handong in Ying Province were made the state of Sui.

sentences.zh: 劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名，備九錫之禮。

translations.literal: He might wear sword and shoes in the palace hall, need not hurry when entering court, need not have his name spoken when praised in obeisance, and was granted the full rites of the Nine Bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: He might wear sword and shoes in the palace hall, need not hurry when entering court, need not have his name spoken when praised in obeisance, and was granted the full rites of the Nine Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 加璽紱、遠遊冠，相國印綠綟綬，位在諸侯王上。

translations.literal: He was given the imperial seal and sash, the cap of distant travel, the chancellor's seal with green tassels and ribbon, and rank above all feudal princes.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the imperial seal and sash, the cap of distant travel, the chancellor's seal with green tassels and ribbon, and rank above all feudal princes.

sentences.zh: 隋國置丞相以下，一依舊式。

translations.literal: Within the state of Sui, a chancellor and subordinate offices were established, all according to the old pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Within the state of Sui, a chancellor and subordinate offices were established, all according to the old pattern.

sentences.zh: 帝再讓，乃受王爵，十郡而已。

translations.literal: The Emperor declined twice and then accepted the royal title with only ten commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor declined twice and then accepted the royal title with only ten commanderies.

sentences.zh: 周帝詔進皇祖、皇考爵並為王，夫人為王妃。

translations.literal: The Zhou emperor issued an edict advancing the imperial grandfather and the late Emperor's father to kings and the lady to princess consort.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor issued an edict advancing the imperial grandfather and the late Emperor's father to kings and the lady to princess consort.

sentences.zh: 大定元年二月壬子，下令曰：「以前賜姓，皆復其舊。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Dading, on the day renzi, an order was issued: "All previously granted surnames are restored to their original ones.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Dading, on the day renzi, an order was issued: "All previously granted surnames are restored to their original ones.

sentences.zh: 」甲寅，帝受九錫之禮。

translations.literal: " On the day jiayin, the Emperor received the rites of the Nine Bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: " On the day jiayin, the Emperor received the rites of the Nine Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，周帝又詔帝冕十有二旒，建天子旌旗；

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, the Zhou emperor again issued an edict granting the Emperor a crown with twelve tassels and establishing the banners of the Son of Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingchen, the Zhou emperor again issued an edict granting the Emperor a crown with twelve tassels and establishing the banners of the Son of Heaven;

sentences.zh: 出警入蹕，乘金根車，駕六馬，備五時副車，置旄頭雲罕；

translations.literal: when going out and returning he was cleared by guards, he rode the golden-root carriage, was drawn by six horses, had five seasonal secondary carriages, and was given banners of maotou and yunhan;
translations.idiomatic: when going out and returning he was cleared by guards, he rode the golden-root carriage, was drawn by six horses, had five seasonal secondary carriages, and was given banners of maotou and yunhan;

sentences.zh: 樂舞八佾，設鐘諄宮縣；

translations.literal: eight rows of dancers performed, and bell chimes and palace music were established;
translations.idiomatic: eight rows of dancers performed, and bell chimes and palace music were established;

sentences.zh: 王妃為王后，世子為太子。

translations.literal: the princess consort became queen and the heir became crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: the princess consort became queen and the heir became crown prince.

sentences.zh: 前後三讓，乃受。

translations.literal: After declining three times, he then accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Three times he declined; only then did he accept.

sentences.zh: 俄而下詔，依唐虞、漢魏故事。

translations.literal: Soon an edict was issued following the precedents of Tang-Yao, Yu-Shun, Han, and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict followed the precedents of Tang-Yao, Yu-Shun, Han, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 帝三讓，不許。

translations.literal: The Emperor declined three times; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor declined three times, but was not allowed to refuse.

sentences.zh: 乃遣太傅、上柱國、巳國公椿奉冊曰：咨爾相國隋王，粵若上古之初。

translations.literal: He then dispatched Grand Tutor, Pillar of State, Duke Chun of Ji to present the register, saying: O Chancellor of State, King of Sui, even as at the beginning of high antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Grand Tutor, Pillar of State, Duke Chun of Ji to present the register, saying: O Chancellor of State, King of Sui, even as at the beginning of high antiquity.

sentences.zh: 爰啟清濁，降符授聖，為天下君；

translations.literal: He opened the clear and the turbid, Heaven sent down the tally and invested the sage, making him ruler of the realm;
translations.idiomatic: He opened the clear and the turbid; Heaven sent down the tally and invested the sage as ruler of the realm;

sentences.zh: 事上帝而理兆庶，和百靈而利萬物；

translations.literal: he served the Supreme Lord and governed the multitudes, harmonized the hundred spirits and benefited the ten thousand things;
translations.idiomatic: he served the Supreme Lord and governed the multitudes, harmonized the hundred spirits, and benefited the ten thousand things;

sentences.zh: 非以區宇之富，未以宸極為尊。

translations.literal: not because the realm was rich, nor because the imperial pinnacle was honored.
translations.idiomatic: not because the realm was rich, nor because the imperial throne was honored.

sentences.zh: 大庭、軒轅以前，驪連、赫胥之日，咸以無為無欲，不將不迎。

translations.literal: Before the Great Court and Yellow Emperor, in the days of Lianxu and Hexu, all took nonaction and no desire, neither bringing nor welcoming.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Great Court and Yellow Emperor, in the days of Lianxu and Hexu, all took nonaction and no desire, neither bringing nor welcoming.

sentences.zh: 遐哉，其詳不可聞已。

translations.literal: How distant! The details cannot be heard.
translations.idiomatic: How remote! The details cannot be heard.

sentences.zh: 厥有載籍，遺文可觀，聖莫逾於堯，美未過於舜。

translations.literal: There are records preserved; surviving texts can be read. No sage surpassed Yao; no beauty exceeded Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Records survive and texts can still be read. No sage surpassed Yao; no beauty exceeded Shun.

sentences.zh: 堯得太尉，已作運衡之篇；

translations.literal: When Yao obtained the Grand Commandant, he already composed the chapter on the celestial balance;
translations.idiomatic: When Yao obtained the Grand Commandant, he already composed the chapter on the celestial balance;

sentences.zh: 舜遇司空，便敘菁華之竭。

translations.literal: when Shun met the Minister of Works, he at once set forth the exhaustion of fine blossoms.
translations.idiomatic: when Shun met the Minister of Works, he at once set forth the exhaustion of fine blossoms.

sentences.zh: 褰裳脫屣，二宮設饗，百官歸禹，若帝之初。

translations.literal: Lifting robe and casting off shoes, the two palaces set out feasts; the hundred officials returned to Yu as at the beginning of the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Lifting robe and casting off shoes, the two palaces set out feasts; the hundred officials returned to Yu as at the beginning of the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 斯蓋上則天時，不敢不授；

translations.literal: This was above in accord with Heaven's seasons and dared not fail to invest;
translations.idiomatic: Above, this accorded with Heaven's seasons and dared not fail to invest;

sentences.zh: 下祗天命，不敢不受。

translations.literal: below it honored Heaven's mandate and dared not fail to receive.
translations.idiomatic: below, it honored Heaven's mandate and dared not fail to receive.

sentences.zh: 湯代於夏，武革於殷，干戈揖讓，雖復異揆，應天順人，其道靡異。

translations.literal: Tang replaced Xia and Wu overthrew Yin; though dry weapons and yielding by bow differed in measure, responding to Heaven and following the people, the Way was not different.
translations.idiomatic: Tang replaced Xia and Wu overthrew Yin; though arms and yielding by bow differed in form, in responding to Heaven and following the people the Way was the same.

sentences.zh: 自漢迄晉，有魏至周，天歷逐獄訟之歸，神鼎隨謳歌之去。

translations.literal: From Han through Jin, from Wei to Zhou, the celestial calendar followed the return of litigation, and the divine cauldron followed the departure of songs of praise.
translations.idiomatic: From Han through Jin, from Wei to Zhou, the celestial calendar followed the return of litigation, and the divine cauldron followed the departure of songs of praise.

sentences.zh: 道高者稱帝，祿盡者不王；

translations.literal: He whose Way was high was called Emperor; when emolument was exhausted he was not king;
translations.idiomatic: He whose Way was high was called Emperor; when emolument was exhausted he was not king;

sentences.zh: 與夫文祖神宗，無以別也。

translations.literal: from the civil ancestors and divine sovereigns there was no distinction.
translations.idiomatic: from the civil ancestors and divine sovereigns there was no distinction.

sentences.zh: 周德將盡，禍難頻興。

translations.literal: Zhou virtue was nearing exhaustion; calamities arose repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou virtue was nearing its end; calamities arose again and again.

sentences.zh: 宗戚奸回，咸將竊發，顧瞻宮闕，將圖宗社。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen and treacherous factions all intended to rise in rebellion, looking toward the palace and plotting the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen and treacherous factions all intended rebellion, eyeing the palace and plotting against the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 籓維連率，逆亂相尋，搖蕩三方，不合如礪。

translations.literal: Frontier commanders and regional leaders followed one another in rebellion and disorder, shaking the three regions and failing to cohere like a whetstone.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier commanders and regional leaders rebelled in succession, shaking the three regions and failing to cohere like a whetstone.

sentences.zh: 蛇行鳥攫，投足無所。

translations.literal: Serpents crawled and birds seized; there was nowhere to set foot.
translations.idiomatic: Serpents crawled and birds seized prey; there was nowhere safe to stand.

sentences.zh: 王受天明命，睿德在躬。

translations.literal: The King received Heaven's bright mandate; sagely virtue was in his person.
translations.idiomatic: The King received Heaven's bright mandate; sagely virtue dwelt in his person.

sentences.zh: 救頹運之艱，匡墜地之業；

translations.literal: He rescued the hardship of a collapsing age and set right a falling enterprise;
translations.idiomatic: He rescued a collapsing age from hardship and set right a falling enterprise;

sentences.zh: 援大川之溺，救燎原之火；

translations.literal: he pulled the drowning from the great river and quenched the fire spreading over the plain;
translations.idiomatic: he pulled the drowning from the great river and quenched the fire spreading over the plain;

sentences.zh: 除群凶於城社，廓妖氣於遠服。

translations.literal: he removed the wicked from the altars of soil and grain and cleared demonic vapors from distant lands.
translations.idiomatic: he removed the wicked from the altars of soil and grain and cleared demonic vapors from distant lands.

sentences.zh: 至德合於造化，神用洽於天壤；

translations.literal: Supreme virtue accorded with creation and transformation; divine efficacy harmonized with Heaven and earth;
translations.idiomatic: Supreme virtue accorded with creation and transformation; divine efficacy harmonized with Heaven and earth;

sentences.zh: 八極九野，萬方四裔，圓首方足，莫不樂推。

translations.literal: the eight extremities and nine wilds, the myriad regions and four frontiers—all with round heads and square feet none failed to rejoice in pushing him forward.
translations.idiomatic: the eight extremities and nine wilds, the myriad regions and four frontiers—all with round heads and square feet rejoiced in pushing him forward.

sentences.zh: 往歲長星夜掃，經天晝見。

translations.literal: In past years the long star swept the night sky and was seen crossing heaven by day.
translations.idiomatic: In past years the long star swept the night sky and was seen crossing heaven by day.

sentences.zh: 八風比夏後之作，五緯同漢帝之聚，除舊之征，昭然在上。

translations.literal: The eight winds matched the work of Xia's successor; the five planets gathered as in Han Emperor's time; the sign of removing the old was clear above.
translations.idiomatic: The eight winds matched the work of Xia's successor; the five planets gathered as in Han Emperor's time; the sign of removing the old was clear above.

sentences.zh: 近者赤雀降祉，玄龜效靈，鐘石變音，蛟魚出穴，有新之貺，煥焉在下。

translations.literal: Recently the red sparrow brought blessing and the dark tortoise showed efficacy; bells and stones changed tone and horned fish emerged from caves; the gift of renewal shone below.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the red sparrow brought blessing and the dark tortoise showed efficacy; bells and stones changed tone and horned fish emerged from caves; the gift of renewal shone below.

sentences.zh: 九區歸往，百靈協贊，人神屬望，我不獨知。

translations.literal: The nine regions turned to him; the hundred spirits joined in praise; men and spirits looked to him—I alone did not know.
translations.idiomatic: The nine regions turned to him; the hundred spirits joined in praise; men and spirits looked to him—I alone did not know.

sentences.zh: 仰祗皇靈，俯順人願，敬以帝位，禪於爾躬。

translations.literal: Looking up to honor the imperial numen and bowing down to follow the people's wish, I respectfully yield the imperial position to your person.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up to honor the imperial numen and bowing down to follow the people's wish, I respectfully yield the imperial position to your person.

sentences.zh: 天祚告窮，天祿永終。

translations.literal: Heaven's favor announces its end; Heaven's emolument ends forever.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's favor announces its end; Heaven's emolument ends forever.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 王其允執厥和，儀刑典訓；

translations.literal: King, earnestly hold to harmony and take the classics as your model;
translations.idiomatic: King, earnestly hold to harmony and take the classics as your model;

sentences.zh: 升圓丘而敬蒼昊，禦皇極而撫黔黎，副率土之心，恢無疆之祚，可不盛歟！

translations.literal: ascend the round mound and reverence the azure Heaven, mount the imperial pinnacle and soothe the black-headed people, fulfill the heart of all within the realm, and extend boundless fortune—can it not be glorious!
translations.idiomatic: ascend the round mound and reverence the azure Heaven, mount the imperial pinnacle and soothe the black-headed people, fulfill the heart of all within the realm, and extend boundless fortune—can it not be glorious!

sentences.zh: 遣大宗伯、大將軍、金城公趙蟹奉皇帝璽紱，百官勸進，帝乃受焉。

translations.literal: He dispatched Grand Director of Ceremonies, Grand General, Duke Zhao of Jincheng to present the imperial seal and sash; the hundred officials urged advancement, and the Emperor then accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Grand Director of Ceremonies, Grand General, Duke Zhao of Jincheng to present the imperial seal and sash; the hundred officials urged advancement, and the Emperor then accepted.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年春二月甲子，自相府常服入宮，備禮即皇帝位於臨光殿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang, in the second month, on the day jiazi, he entered the palace from the chancellor's office in ordinary dress and, with full rites, took the imperial throne at Lingguang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year one, second month, on jiazi day, he entered the palace from the chancellor's office in ordinary dress and, with full rites, took the imperial throne at Lingguang Hall.

sentences.zh: 設壇於南郊，遣兼太傅、上柱國、鄧公竇熾柴燎告天。

translations.literal: An altar was set at the southern suburb, and Acting Grand Tutor, Pillar of State, Duke Chi of Deng was dispatched to burn firewood and report to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: An altar was set at the southern suburb, and Acting Grand Tutor, Pillar of State, Duke Chi of Deng was sent to burn firewood and report to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 是日，告廟。

translations.literal: That day, he reported to the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: That day he reported to the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the reign title was changed.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the reign title was changed.

sentences.zh: 京師慶雲見。

translations.literal: Auspicious clouds appeared in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious clouds appeared over the capital.

sentences.zh: 改周官，依漢、魏之舊。

translations.literal: The Zhou official system was changed to follow Han and Wei precedents.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou official system was changed to follow Han and Wei precedents.

sentences.zh: 制：以相國司馬高譫為尚書左僕射兼納言，相國司錄虞慶則為內史監兼史部尚書，相國內郎李德林為內史令，上開府韋世康為禮部尚書，上開府元暉為都官尚書，開府、戶部尚書元巖為兵部尚書，上儀同、司宗長孫毗為工部尚書，上儀同、司會楊尚希為度支尚書，雍州牧楊惠為左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Regulations: Chancellor of State Chief of Staff Gao Jiong was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief; Chancellor of State Recorder Yu Qingze was made Director of the Palace Secretariat and Concurrent Director of the Ministry of Personnel; Chancellor of State Internal Gentleman Li Delin was made Director of the Palace Secretariat; Upper Palace Gate General Wei Shikang was made Director of the Ministry of Rites; Upper Palace Gate General Yuan Hui was made Director of the Ministry of Justice; Palace Gate General, Director of the Ministry of Revenue Yuan Yan was made Director of the Ministry of War; Upper Third Rank Equivalent, Director of the Imperial Clan Sun Pi was made Director of the Ministry of Works; Upper Third Rank Equivalent, Director of Accounts Yang Shangxi was made Director of the Ministry of Taxation; Governor of Yong Province Yang Hui was made General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations: Gao Jiong, Chief of Staff to the Chancellor of State, became Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief; Yu Qingze, Recorder to the Chancellor of State, became Director of the Palace Secretariat and Concurrent Director of the Ministry of Personnel; Li Delin, Internal Gentleman to the Chancellor of State, became Director of the Palace Secretariat; Upper Palace Gate General Wei Shikang became Director of the Ministry of Rites; Upper Palace Gate General Yuan Hui became Director of the Ministry of Justice; Palace Gate General and Director of the Ministry of Revenue Yuan Yan became Director of the Ministry of War; Upper Third Rank Equivalent and Director of the Imperial Clan Sun Pi became Director of the Ministry of Works; Upper Third Rank Equivalent and Director of Accounts Yang Shangxi became Director of the Ministry of Taxation; and Governor of Yong Province Yang Hui became General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，追尊皇考為武元皇帝，廟號太祖；

translations.literal: On the day yichou, the late Emperor's father was posthumously honored as Emperor Wuyuan, with temple name Taizu;
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day the late Emperor's father was posthumously honored as Emperor Wuyuan, with temple name Taizu;

sentences.zh: 皇妣呂氏為元明皇后。

translations.literal: the imperial mother Lady Lü was made Empress Yuanming.
translations.idiomatic: the imperial mother Lady Lü was made Empress Yuanming.

sentences.zh: 改周氏左社右廟制為右社左廟。
